Since fall 2019, the project country has been experiencing one of the worst socio-economic crises in the world. The countrys currency has lost around 98% of its value, while prices for essential goods, including food, have risen by more than 1,000%. According to the United Nations “Humanitarian Crisis Analysis 2024”, the majority of the population is unable to meet their basic needs. More and more people are resorting to negative coping mechanisms, such as restricting food consumption or cutting spending on education and health.
